<p dir="auto">Drive native desktop apps <strong>in the background</strong>. Agents click, type, and verify without stealing the cursor or focus. Use the same CLI and MCP server on macOS, Windows, and Linux from Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenClaw, and custom clients. <p dir="auto">Create and manage macOS/Linux VMs with near-native performance on Apple Silicon using Apple's Virtualization.Framework.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# Install Lume
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/lume/install.sh)"

# Create and start a vanilla macOS VM from an Apple restore image
curl -L "$(lume ipsw | tail -n 1)" -o ~/Downloads/macos-tahoe.ipsw
lume create macos-tahoe --ipsw ~/Downloads/macos-tahoe.ipsw --unattended tahoe
lume run macos-tahoe"><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Install Lume</span>
/bin/bash -c <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">$(</span>curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/lume/install.sh<span class="pl-pds">)</span></span><span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Create and start a vanilla macOS VM from an Apple restore image</span>
curl -L <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span><span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">$(</span>lume ipsw <span class="pl-k">|</span> tail -n 1<span class="pl-pds">)</span></span><span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> -o <span class="pl-k">~</span>/Downloads/macos-tahoe.ipsw
lume create macos-tahoe --ipsw <span class="pl-k">~</span>/Downloads/macos-tahoe.ipsw --unattended tahoe
lume run macos-tahoe</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The <code>--unattended</code> option prepares the installed guest offline. The built-in
<code>sequoia</code> and <code>tahoe</code> presets create the <code>lume</code> user, enable SSH, configure
autologin, and disable sleep and screen locking. The default credentials are
<code>lume</code> / <code>lume</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">The Tahoe flow is E2E verified. Sequoia may still open the Accessibility step
of Setup Assistant on its first display boot; see <a href="https://github.com/trycua/cua/issues/2155" data-hovercard-type="issue" data-hovercard-url="/trycua/cua/issues/2155/hovercard">issue #2155</a>.</p>
